title: Constructing Exotic Calabi–Yau 3-Folds via Quantum Inner State Manifolds
content: We introduce a novel construction of exotic Calabi–Yau threefolds (and higher-dimensional analogues) by employing a new geometric tool called \emph{Quantum Inner State Manifolds} (QISM). Building on established topological surgeries in symplectic geometry—such as Luttinger surgeries on tori, Gompf’s symplectic fiber sums, and Lefschetz pencil techniques—we show how QISMs can be integrated into these frameworks to produce smooth manifolds with vanishing first Chern class that are nontrivial in topology. We formulate the QISM as a fibration of quantum state spaces (e.g.\ projective Hilbert spaces of internal degrees of freedom) over a base manifold, endowing the total space with a Kähler-like structure inherited from the Fubini–Study form. By carefully matching the Chern classes of base and fiber (analogous to taking K3$\times T^2$ or other known CY factors) and performing coisotropic Luttinger surgeries generalized to QISM fibers, we obtain families of simply-connected six-manifolds with $c_1=0$ and exotic smooth structure. We discuss the relation of this construction to mirror symmetry and string compactification, comparing with known symplectic Calabi–Yau examples. Our results suggest new avenues for finding compactifications with novel moduli and dualities in string/quantum gravity contexts.
